meta.title: Acme 2026 Growth Strategy
meta.subtitle: Recommendation to the Board
meta.governing_thought: Acme should move upmarket to enterprise HR in 2026, funded by sunsetting the SMB tier — adding an estimated $40M ARR over 24 months.

slides.title: Acme should move upmarket to enterprise HR in 2026, funded by sunsetting SMB — adding an estimated $40M ARR over 24 months
supporting_points: Growth has stalled at 3% for two years while three competitors have grown 25%+ by moving upmarket
The enterprise segment is $4.2B and growing 18% — three times our current addressable market
Two of our top-30 customers already use Acme above 500 employees and would expand within 12 months
The product gap to enterprise-ready is six features, deliverable in three quarters with current capacity
The SMB tier costs $14M annually to serve and is contribution-margin negative in 60% of accounts
slides.source: Strategy team analysis; Acme financials FY24

slides.title: Growth has stalled at 3% for two years while three competitors have grown 25%+
slides.framing_line: Based on Acme financials FY23–FY24 and competitor 10-K filings (n=3 peers)
bullets: Acme revenue grew 3% in FY23 and 3% in FY24 — flat against a market growing 11% annually
The three largest competitors each grew 25%+ over the same period, gaining 6pp of combined share
The gap concentrates in enterprise accounts, where Acme win rates trail the leaders by 18pp
slides.source: Acme financials FY23–FY24; competitor 10-K filings; team analysis

slides.title: Growth has stalled at 3% for two years while three competitors have grown 25%+ by moving upmarket
bullets: Acme ARR has grown ~3% in both years (3.1% FY23, 3.4% FY24), versus a five-year average of 14%
Three named competitors have each grown 25%+ annually, crossing $300M ARR by adding enterprise tiers since 2023
Net revenue retention has fallen from 118% to 102% over the same period
Customer count has grown, but average contract value has compressed by 11%

slides.title: Three of our five product lines fall in the low-growth, low-margin quadrant
slides.source: Acme product P&L FY24; market growth from Gartner 2024

slides.title: We evaluated four growth paths against three criteria; only enterprise expansion meets all three

slides.title: Enterprise expansion is the only option that scores high on market size, fit, and feasibility
The path to enterprise-ready spans four sequential capabilities, deliverable in three quarters

steps.name: API platform
steps.description: Public APIs and webhooks at SLA

slides.quote: Acme has the best mid-market HR product we've used. The day they support our European subsidiaries, we'll triple our spend.
slides.attribution: VP People, Top-10 Acme customer (1,200 employees)

slides.title: Combined: enterprise expansion adds $40M ARR by end-2027; sunsetting SMB frees $14M to fund it
slides.placeholder_text: [ Waterfall chart: FY25 ARR → +Enterprise → +Existing expansion → −SMB churn → FY27 ARR ]
slides.caption: Net new ARR of +$26M, plus $14M annual cost savings from SMB sunset, for a total $40M EBITDA improvement.

slides.title: Implementation in three phases over 18 months, with the SMB sunset starting in Q2 2026
slides.framing_line: 18-month plan, Q2 2026 through H1 2027; owners per milestone in the appendix

slides.title: Key risks and mitigations span three categories: sales cycle, customer churn, and competitive response
bullets: Enterprise sales cycle (6–9 months): mitigated by leveraging existing top-30 accounts as anchor customers
SMB churn during sunset: mitigated by 18-month transition period and partner referral program
Competitive response: mitigated by 9-month feature lead and existing customer relationships
slides.source: Risk review with executive team, March 2026
